shared_elements: T-shaped/anthropomorphic upright pillar with a broad head and narrower shaft
low-relief motifs carved on the broad flat face
arms/limb-like elements running down the sides and bending toward the front
stacked registers of motifs read vertically down the slab
animal or serpentine forms rendered in flat silhouette relief
justification: Both surfaces are the same distinctive kind of object-as-image: a broad-headed anthropomorphic upright slab whose flat face carries stacked registers of flat, silhouette-style low relief, with limb-like elements descending the sides and curving toward the front, and small creature/serpentine forms among the motifs. The difference is in the specific content: A shows a clearly readable menagerie (a row of quadrupeds above a chevron band, birds, a long-necked bird, a fox-like animal), while B's carving is dominated by narrow vertical strap-like bands and indistinct hanging figures with looping forms at the base, so no single identical motif can be matched between them.
